cards.explanation: The answer is nurse. Jehosheba, King Joram's daughter and Ahaziah's sister, takes little Joash and puts him and his nurse in a bedroom. The text says she did it to hide him from Athaliah, Ahaziah's mother. I think this one is heavy, with the king's sons being murdered all around. But the verse ends with “…and he was not killed.” (2 Kings 11:2)

The answer is the house of the LORD. Joash remained hidden with his nurse in the house of the LORD for six years while Athaliah ruled the land. Six years is a long time to stay tucked away, friends. The text puts him right there in the house of the LORD.
The answer is True. The text says Joash remained hidden for six years while Athaliah ruled the land. So there's a ruler on the throne, and a little king-to-be tucked away where she can't reach him.

The answer is Joash, the king's son. Jehoiada the priest shows the commanders the king's son, and that's Joash, Ahaziah's little boy. He does it after making a covenant with them and putting them under oath. After six years of Joash staying hidden, those commanders get to see him. I bet they had a lot to think about in that moment.

The answer is that they must be put to death. Jehoiada says, “…anyone who approaches the ranks must be put to death.” (2 Kings 11:8) He is not playing around, friends. The king is surrounded, weapons in hand, and the ranks are off limits.
The answer is True. Jehoiada says, “You must stay close to the king wherever he goes.” (2 Kings 11:8) That's an order to surround him with weapons in hand. Where Joash goes, the guards stay close.

The answer is David. Jehoiada gives the commanders the spears and shields of King David from the house of the LORD. Those weapons were in the house of the LORD, and now they go to the commanders. Jehoiada the priest is the one handing them out.

The answer is the crown. Jehoiada brings out the king's son and puts the crown on him. That's Joash, Ahaziah's little boy, the one who's been hidden for six years. That's quite a way to go from the bedroom to a crowned head.

The answer is that they anoint him. After Jehoiada crowns Joash, gives him the Testimony and proclaims him king, they anoint him. The crown, the Testimony, the proclamation and the anointing all pile up in one verse. I think that's a lot to take in for a seven-year-old, but he's got a crowd cheering him on.

The answer is False. The text says the people clapped their hands and declared, “Long live the king!” (2 Kings 11:12) That's clapping and shouting, not silence. After all that hiding, the quiet is over.

The answer is the new king. Athaliah looks out and sees the king standing by the pillar, according to the custom. That's Joash, the one crowned in the house of the LORD. I think this is a rough moment for her.

The answer is Treason. Athaliah tears her clothes and screams, “Treason! Treason!” (2 Kings 11:14) She says it twice, and loud. That's what she hollers when she sees the king crowned and the people rejoicing.

The answer is False. The text says, “She must not be put to death in the house of the LORD.” (2 Kings 11:15) So Jehoiada orders the commanders to bring her out between the ranks. The place matters to him, and he says so plainly.

The answer is the horses' entrance to the palace grounds. The commanders seize Athaliah as she reaches the horses' entrance to the palace grounds, and there she is put to death. That's outside the house of the LORD, just as Jehoiada ordered. The text gives the exact spot.

The answer is that they would be the LORD's people. Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people that they would be the LORD's people. That's the heart of it, and it's the biggest promise in the whole scene. It's more than a crown, friends. It's a promise about who they belong to.

The answer is True. Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, and he also makes a covenant between the king and the people. That's two covenants, one right after the other. The man was busy that day.
The answer is idols. The people of the land go to the temple of Baal and tear it down. They smash the altars and idols to pieces. I bet that made some noise.

The answer is the throne. They enter the royal palace by way of the Gate of the Guards, and then Joash takes his seat on the royal throne. From a hidden bedroom to the royal throne. That's a big move for one little king.

The answer is False. The text says all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet because Athaliah had been put to the sword at the royal palace. So after the shouting and the trumpets, the city settles down. Quiet at last.

The answer is seven years old. The text says, “Joash was seven years old when he became king.” (2 Kings 11:21) Before this, he spent six years hidden with his nurse in the house of the LORD. Now he takes the throne.
